elements.element: No non-compete restriction applies to Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 expressly states that nothing restricts Customer's development, acquisition, licensing, sale, or use of any product or service and confirms that Customer has made no non-compete commitment. Section 12.4 is permissive rather than prohibitory.

elements.element: No field-of-use restriction applies to Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 expressly permits Customer to conduct business in any field or territory.

elements.element: Any non-compete restriction is limited to a named competing product.
elements.evidence: The condition is absent: the rendered clause imposes no non-compete restriction at all, as confirmed by Section 12.3 and the permissive language in Section 12.4.

elements.element: Any non-compete restriction applies only during the term.
elements.evidence: The condition is absent because no non-compete restriction is imposed. The reference to the term and the following 24 months modifies an affirmative permission, not a prohibition.

elements.element: Any non-compete restriction lasts no more than 12 months.
elements.evidence: The condition is absent because the rendered language imposes no non-compete restriction or restricted duration.

elements.element: Any non-compete restriction carves out Customer's internal development.
elements.evidence: The condition is absent; moreover, Sections 12.3 and 12.4 affirmatively permit Customer to develop competing products or services.

elements.element: Any non-compete restriction carves out Customer's acquisitions.
elements.evidence: The condition is absent; moreover, Sections 12.3 and 12.4 affirmatively permit Customer to acquire competing products or services.

result.reason: The operative redline eliminates the original non-compete by changing Section 12.4 from a prohibition to a permission, while Section 12.3 independently and unequivocally disclaims non-compete and field-of-use restrictions. It therefore satisfies the preferred position and, because no restriction remains, exceeds the fallback protections. The edit is minimal and does not alter unrelated commercial terms. Drafting quality is slightly reduced because retaining the temporal phrase in a permissive Section 12.4 is unnecessary and could invite a weak negative implication after the stated period, although Section 12.3 resolves that issue.
